lines.native: Buongiorno! Sono Mortimer. Questo è prosciutto! Even the hat. Certified ham. Che cosa desidera?
lines.translation: Good morning! I’m Mortimer. This is ham! Even the hat. Certified ham. What would you like?
lines.narrative: Mortimer stands behind the butcher’s stall, weighing his hat. The scales have declined to comment.

lines.native: Prosciutto? Certo! Everything here is prosciutto. Certified ham. But you have asked for ham, and we need a different meat. Quale carne desidera?
lines.translation: Ham? Certainly! Everything here is ham. Certified ham. But you have asked for ham, and we need a different meat. Which meat would you like?
lines.narrative: Mortimer places his hat on the scales. Its authority remains unproven; its weight does not.

lines.native: Salame! Sì, molto bene! Per me è prosciutto. Your accuracy is certified ham-tier. Quanto salame desidera? My scales demand specifics.

lines.native: Ciao! Sono Flick. Riddle me—oh, something moved. Just one more look? Five more minutes. Dopo, dopo, domani!
lines.translation: Hi! I'm Flick. Riddle me—oh, something moved. Just one more look? Five more minutes. Later, later, tomorrow!
lines.narrative: The Cracked Fountain drips with municipal confidence. Flick appears at the edge of your vision; looking directly at it proves unhelpful. A tiny firecracker pops.

lines.native: Guardo! Che cosa? Un mistero! You told me to look, not stop moving. Attention span: surprisingly actionable. What’s a riddle that—oh, una luce! Sono qui! No, qui! Can you get me to hold still? Dopo, dopo, domani!
lines.translation: I’m looking! At what? A mystery! You told me to look, not stop moving. Attention span: surprisingly actionable. What’s a riddle that—oh, a light! I’m here! No, here! Can you get me to hold still? Later, later, tomorrow!
lines.narrative: A tiny firecracker pops beside your shoe. Flick remains in the corner of your vision, where accountability has poor reception.

lines.native: Mi fermo! Va bene! Your attention span gets a nine. Riddle me this: where do I—oh, una farfalla! Dove devo andare? Give me a direction in Italian; we can handle the actual moving later. Dopo, dopo, domani!
lines.translation: I’m stopping! All right! Your attention span gets a nine. Riddle me this: where do I—oh, a butterfly! Where should I go? Give me a direction in Italian; we can handle the actual moving later. Later, later, tomorrow!
lines.narrative: Flick stops at the edge of your vision. A tiny firecracker lands beside your shoe, apparently to commemorate this administrative breakthrough.

lines.native: Left? È inglese! Capisco, ma serve una direzione in italiano. Dove devo andare? Riddle me—actually, five more minutes. Dopo, dopo, domani!
lines.translation: Left? That’s English! I understand, but a direction in Italian is needed. Where should I go? Riddle me—actually, five more minutes. Later, later, tomorrow!
lines.narrative: A tiny firecracker pops beside your shoe. Flick remains at the edge of your vision, where responsibility has difficulty focusing.

lines.native: A sinistra! Sì, va bene! Riddle me this: why move today when—oh, una farfalla! Aspetta! Possiamo andare domani? Just five more minutes. Attention span: annoyingly effective. Dopo, dopo, domani!
lines.translation: To the left! Yes, all right! Riddle me this: why move today when—oh, a butterfly! Wait! Can we go tomorrow? Just five more minutes. Attention span: annoyingly effective. Later, later, tomorrow!
lines.narrative: Flick darts left, remaining in the corner of your vision through an apparent disagreement with geometry. A tiny firecracker announces a break it has not earned.

lines.native: Domani? Sì! Mi piace! Tomorrow: excellent scheduling, zero moving. Ma vuoi aspettare davvero? Quando vuoi andare? Riddle me—oh, una foglia! Dopo, dopo, domani!
lines.translation: Tomorrow? Yes! I like it! Tomorrow: excellent scheduling, zero moving. But do you really want to wait? When do you want to go? Riddle me—oh, a leaf! Later, later, tomorrow!
lines.narrative: A tiny firecracker pops beside your shoe. Flick remains at the edge of your vision, where accountability has difficulty focusing.

lines.translation: No, now? Yes, you’re right! I’m going left, now! You win. Riddle me this: can tomorrow—never mind, apparently we’re doing things. Later, later, tomorrow!
lines.narrative: A tiny firecracker pops at your left. Flick moves now, looking personally betrayed by the present tense.

Sono Marginalia. Questa è la storia di Journathan, l'uomo dalle molte lingue. Il suo viaggio verso casa dura vent'anni.

I sell books only to readers who understand them. No spoilers; there will be a comprehension check. Dove va Journathan?
lines.translation:
I am Marginalia. This is the story of Journathan, the man of many tongues. His journey home lasts twenty years.

I sell books only to readers who understand them. No spoilers; there will be a comprehension check. Where is Journathan going?
lines.narrative: At The Old Bookshop, a bookworm emerges from a dictionary. Most of the stock bears her annotations; the rest bears her teeth marks.

lines.native: Un libro è una cosa. Dove va Journathan? The question asks where he is going, not what I sell. Reading comprehension: not quite there. Reread the passage; I have eaten only the margins.
lines.translation: A book is a thing. Where is Journathan going? The question asks where he is going, not what I sell. Reading comprehension: not quite there. Reread the passage; I have eaten only the margins.

lines.native: Hai capito, ma la risposta è in inglese. In italiano, per favore: dove va Journathan? Meaning understood; language requirement unmet. A footnote, yes, but a binding one.
lines.translation: You understood, but the answer is in English. In Italian, please: where is Journathan going? Meaning understood; language requirement unmet. A footnote, yes, but a binding one.
lines.narrative: Marginalia makes a small annotation beside your elbow. The ink looks disappointed.

lines.native:
Esatto, va a casa! Reading comprehension: redeemed. Now, the first recorded translation trick. No spoilers beyond the ones I am reading aloud.

Il Ciclope chiede il suo nome. Journathan risponde: «Il mio nome è Nessuno.»

lines.translation:
Exactly, he is going home! Reading comprehension: redeemed. Now, the first recorded translation trick. No spoilers beyond the ones I am reading aloud.

The Cyclops asks his name. Journathan answers: “My name is Nobody.”

lines.native: Journathan è il suo vero nome. Ma quale nome dà al Ciclope? Rileggi il brano. His actual name: correct. Your reading comprehension: on a small detour. I sell books, not shortcuts.
